session_read: Monday 04:xx ET pre-open, gate AMBIGUOUS -- a VIX pop (+4.77%, 14.25->14.93) that disqualified STABILIZING outright while nothing else in the gate fired hot: futures positive, all three Asia indices green, SMH only -0.22%. Friday's session underneath it was messier than the index tape let on: AMAT -5.1% and AVGO -5.9% both cratered, but for different reasons -- AMAT was routine pre-earnings de-risking, AVGO was a real one. BofA cut Broadcom's BOND rating over the off-balance-sheet XPV financing platform it built with Blackstone and Apollo to fund Anthropic compute -- stress-test exposure to $370bn at the full 2028 buildout, a ~$42bn extreme-loss case -- in the same call it RAISED AVGO's FY26 revenue and EBITDA numbers. That is a financing-structure verdict sitting on top of an unchanged fundamental one, and it lands on AVGO and BX together, 5.19% of the book. BX was already an overbought trim candidate on RSI alone; the financing read is a second, independent reason to take a little more off, not a reason to touch AVGO, which still sits in the accumulate bucket with a strengthening thesis and no trigger of its own. Monday's pre-market shows the book recovering broadly -- SNDK +6%, MU +3.8%, SKHY +4.3%, everything ext_hr-positive -- which the catalyst desk reads as AI-optimism momentum continuation, not a fresh catalyst, and sentiment agrees: 81.8, extreme_greed, unchanged band, action_hint still 'propose profit-booking on overweight/breach names.' Nothing in the book moved on its own this run -- no trades, no thesis changes, no earnings inside five sessions -- so the work was entirely about re-pricing what was already open: three of twelve proposals (BX, NBIS, CEG) got fresh rationale and one got resized, MU picked up a new stop-raise now that it is up 15% against a stop that sits below breakeven, and cash is still $12 against a five-figure book. Ten names remain over their own ATR cap, aggregate open risk 14.8% against a 10% budget, and the only cluster out of band is Compute/Hyperscaler, sitting 9.65 points under its floor with no obvious name left to fill it -- MSFT's own overbought trim deepens that hole rather than curing anything, which the desk is doing anyway because the RSI reason stands on its own.
